content.en: In an earlier edition of the Newsletter (May 1988), we gave a report on 'Child Murder: Police Inaction Continues'. This is to update our readers on the situation in Anand Parbat.

Initially, many efforts were made to persuade the authorities that some action was needed against the SHO of the Anand Parbat Police Station, but our letters to the Lt. Governor, the Commissioner of Police, the Crimes against Women Cell and various other departments of the police, went unheeded. It almost seemed as if the culprit of the case was being given total protection. We had heard that the SHO has been suspended but he was sighted at a post in Palam Airport - as for the reports that he had been arrested, these were a little difficult to believe, because Kamlesh came with accounts of how the man had been seen by her in Anand Parbat on more than one occasion.

Meanwhile, volunteers had checked up in the hospital where Naresh had been admitted, and the existence of 'Medical Records' was confirmed. We visited the hospital and were assured that such a file indeed existed, but it was a 'Top Security' file and we were not permitted to examine it. Armed with this information, we consulted our lawyers, and on their advice, a public interest Litigation was filed in the Supreme Court before the vacation judge, who admitted the case and issued an order that the medical records be placed under seal in the Supreme Court.
As soon as the Supreme Court reopened after the vacation, Kamlesh's case was heard and immediate steps were taken to ensure that: -

en.text: Maya Devi (Kamlesh's neighbour) was reinstated in her room.
The disconnected electric and water supply would be restored.
Kamlesh's belongings would be returned to her.
All charges against Kamlesh would be stayed temporarily.

content.en: Even though these orders were clearly passed by the Court, it took a long time for them to be implemented. Mean- time, Kamlesh was attending hearings regularly. Alongside these hearings, a police investigation was started - a type of cross examination of Kamlesh's evidence was carried out. During these, a volunteer from Saheli was always present.

Maya Devi was given back the tenancy of her room in October 1988. The electricity and water supply has very recently been reconnected (Dec.1988) but the summons for Kamlesh to appear in the lower court did not stop. Nor has the police harassment stopped. Right till now she is visited at her home by members of the police force, and various summons are being served on her.

The criminal cases against the SHO are also going on simultaneously in the lower court. Meanwhile, we have asked that Kamlesh should get complete compensation for the great loss she has had in Naresh's untimely death, and the indignities she has suffered on her person, and also for the life of fear she has been leading since November 1987.
Note: The co-petitioners in the case filed in November 87 were Action India, Ankur, Shakti Shalini, Mrinal Pande (individual) and others.
